la:noun:saxum.gloss: stone, rock (a large, rough fragment of rock)
senses: stone, rock (a large, rough fragment of rock)
la:noun:saxum.html:
saxum (in inscrr. also SAKSVM; from collat. form saxus;
a vocative SAXE,), i, n.
root sak-; Sanscr. ska; cf. secare
, any large, rough stone; a detached fragment of rock; a rock (in gen.; whereas rupes is a steep rock, crag, cliff).
In gen., ; cf. : non est e saxo sculptus,: pars ludicre saxa Jactant, inter se licitantur, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 76 Vahl.): (Sisyphum) adverso nixantem trudere monte Saxum, etc.,: miser impendens magnum timet aëre saxum Tantalus,: saxo cere comminuit brum, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 586 Vahl.); cf.: si glebis aut saxis aut fustibus aliquem de fundo praecipitem egeris,: magni ponderis saxa, in muro collocare,; cf. fin.; 7, 23; 7, 46: (Thyestes) summis saxis fixus asperis, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 413 Vahl.); cf.: aspicite religatum asperis Vinctumque saxis (Prometheum), Cic. poët. Tusc. 2, 10, 23: speluncas saxis pendentibu' structas,; cf., of the cave of Cacus: jam primum saxis suspensam hanc aspice rupem,: tot congesta manu praeruptis oppida saxis,: inter saxa rupesque,: saxa spargens tabo, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 414 Vahl.): vesco sale saxa peresa,: nec turbida ponti Aequora fligebant naves ad saxa,: si ad saxum quo capessit, et saep.: lapis non saxum est,.—In apposition: in saxis silicibus uberiores aquae sunt,in limestone rocks,.—
Prov.
Saxum volvere, i. e. to strive or endeavor in vain (alluding to the stone of Sisyphus): satis diu hoc jam saxum volvo,.—
Inter sacrum saxumque stare; v. sacrum, A. 2. b.—
In partic.
For Saxum Tarpejum (cf. Müll. and v. Tarpejus, II.), the Tarpeian Rock: horribilis de saxo jactus,; ; ; ; ; ; ; v. Tarpeius.—
Saxum sacrum, the sacred rock on the Aventine, at which Remus consulted the auspices, ; called saxum alone,.—
A superior kind of Cimolian chalk (creta Cimolia), .—
Saxa Rubra; v. ruber, II. B.—
Transf.
Plur.: saxa, stony ground, rocky places: mitis in apricis coquitur vindemia saxis,: Ligurum,.—
A stone wall: Romulus saxo lucum circumdedit alto,.—
The strong foundation of a building: Capitolium quadrato saxo substructum,.
